#1233. US science academy urges journals to fix errors more quickly

Thank you for visiting nature.com. You are using a browser version with limited support for CSS. To obtain the best experience, we recommend you use a more up to date browser (or turn off compatibility mode in Internet Explorer). In the meantime, to ensure continued support, we are displaying the site without styles and JavaScript.

A statue of Albert Einstein holding a scientific manuscript sits outside the US National Academy of Sciences building in Washington DC.Credit: Paul J. Richards/AFP via Getty

Update: After a delay, the report discussed in this story was released by the US National Academies of Sciences, Engineering and Medicine on 24 November. The academies said that the problem was with erroneous references added to the report in response to peer review.

Science publishers take too long to retract or correct research papers, a report by the US National Academies of Sciences, Engineering, and Medicine (NASEM) finds. Standards for fixing errors are also inconsistently applied across journals, it says.

Why retractions data could be a powerful tool for cleaning up science

Why retractions data could be a powerful tool for cleaning up science

There are no data on how long a retraction or correction currently takes, because journals do not generally disclose when they were alerted to underlying problems; the NASEM report says that they should start doing this. On average, according to the Retraction Watch database, retractions occur around 2.4 years after a paper is published. The report recommends that, in most cases, editorial review processes be completed within 12 weeks, and should rarely stretch beyond 6 months — at least when editors are looking at concerns over a single paper.

“The big picture is, the process is too slow,” says Randy Schekman, a cell biologist at the University of California, Berkeley, who chaired the 13-person committee that produced the NASEM report. A prompter and more transparent process would strengthen the reliability of the scientific record, he says.

The report was due to be published online on 19 November but was delayed after journalists at Science noted that it contained some references with fabricated first names for authors, a possible sign that large language models had been used to write or edit the material and that it had been insufficiently checked.

“It’s unfortunate that there were these flawed references in a report about fixing the literature,” says Jennifer Byrne, a cancer researcher and research-integrity sleuth at the University of Sydney in Australia, who first flagged the concern to Science when reviewing the report, which was shared ahead of publication with media outlets.

The report had two main aims: to speed up the process of retraction or correction and to lower the “tremendous emotional barriers” for authors to correct honest mistakes in the record, Schekman says. “Part of the problem is that it’s too rare for a paper to be retracted,” he adds.

Retractions of old papers are on the rise: when should bad science be culled?

Retractions of old papers are on the rise: when should bad science be culled?

It also suggests that journals shouldn’t wait for complaints to reach them, but instead “take proactive steps” to identify errors and integrity issues. These might include journal-wide audits, or regularly monitoring social-media feeds and online platforms where post-publication issues are raised, it says.

Existing guidelines for publishers, such as those from the Committee on Publication Ethics (COPE) in London, urge only a “timely” response to concerns1, without setting out expected schedules, and don’t suggest that journals scan online platforms for complaints.

“A major theme running through the report is that we have to distinguish between retraction or correction, and research misconduct,” notes Dorothy Bishop, a research-integrity sleuth in Oxford, UK, who was on the NASEM committee. Authors shouldn’t associate a retraction with the stigma of research misconduct, she says. And although journal editors sometimes wait for a university to investigate whether there is misconduct before correcting a paper, they shouldn’t, she adds.

More than 10,000 research papers were retracted in 2023 — a new record

More than 10,000 research papers were retracted in 2023 — a new record

Calls for changing these attitudes aren’t new: journals have long emphasized that retractions can result from honest mistakes. In a 2022 editorial, Holden Thorp, the editor in chief of Science, urged that the processes of issuing corrections or retractions and making a determination of misconduct should be kept separate2, and COPE guidelines already emphasize the point. But “there are still plenty of people who see a correction or retraction as an allegation of fraud”, says Thorp, who was also on the NASEM committee. “Hopefully, this report will accelerate the recognition of the distinction,” he says.

doi: https://doi.org/10.1038/d41586-026-03787-5

COPE Council. Guidelines: Retraction Guidelines (Committee on Publication Ethics, 2025).

Chelsea are reportedly considering Cesc Fabregas as a replacement for Xabi Alonso, although the former Blues midfielder is unwilling to take charge mid-season.

According to a Football Insider report, the Como manager is among Chelsea’s leading candidates if they decide to part ways with Alonso after their recent struggles.

The 39-year-old has impressed considerably in Italy, attracting attention from several major European clubs after establishing himself as an exciting young managerial prospect.

Fabregas is understood to be keen on taking charge of a major European club in the future, but he would prefer to make such a move during the summer transfer window.

The Spaniard reportedly wants an entire pre-season to implement his tactical ideas and build a team in line with his footballing philosophy. Chelsea would therefore face a potential wait if they decide to pursue their former midfielder.

Como are also reluctant to lose their manager during the campaign, particularly with the Italian side competing in both Serie A and the Champions League.

Meanwhile, Alonso’s position at Stamford Bridge has grown increasingly uncomfortable after a disappointing run of results.

Chelsea are determined to secure Champions League qualification, and failing to stay in the race could put Alonso’s future in serious doubt.

Fabregas could eventually emerge as an attractive appointment, but Chelsea may need to wait until the end of the season for a realistic chance to bring him back to Stamford Bridge.

#1231. Champions League line-ups: Manchester City vs. Napoli

Napoli have a growing injury crisis, but start Kevin De Bruyne, Scott McTominay and Rasmus Hojlund away to Gianluigi Donnarumma and Enzo Maresca’s Manchester City.

It kicks off at the Etihad in Manchester at 20.00 GMT (21.00 CET).

You can follow all the build-up and action as it happens from this game and Como vs. AEK Athens on the Champions League Liveblog.

The Partenopei are struggling badly this season, and confidence was only slightly boosted by a 1-0 win over Torino at the weekend, which left them eighth in the Serie A table.

They risk early European elimination for the second year running, having managed one win and three defeats so far.

Max Allegri’s injury crisis keeps getting worse, with Antonio Vergara, Benoit Badiashile, Alex Meret, Stanislav Lobotka, Giovanni Di Lorenzo, Alisson Santos, Alessandro Buongiorno and suspended Rafa Marin unavailable.

It means the 3-5-1-1 formation is used again, but Noa Lang is used in support of lone striker Hojlund, dropping both De Bruyne and McTominay into midfield, leaving Andre Frank Zambo Anguissa on the bench.

Matias Olivera has to turn into a makeshift central defender, with Matteo Politano and Leonardo Spinazzola out wide.

Manchester City are seventh in the Champions League table after winning three of the first four matches, losing 4-2 at home to trophy holders Paris Saint-Germain.

However, their recent Premier League form has been dismal, scraping one point from four rounds, and coach Maresca must keep an eye on the upcoming clash with Arsenal.

Matheus Nunes and Marc Guehi have shaken off knocks to be in the squad, meaning the only absentee is Antoine Semenyo.

Erling Haaland remains deadly in attack, with support from Juventus transfer target Rayan Cherki, but Ilman Ndiaye and Jeremy Doku are rested ahead of Arsenal, as is captain Ruben Dias.

Italy international Donnarumma has been facing criticism for his performances in goal.

Manchester City beat Napoli here 2-0 last season when Di Lorenzo was sent off after just 21 minutes, prompting Antonio Conte to substitute De Bruyne against his former club.

The Belgian veteran will be hoping to make more of an impact here this time around.

Manchester City: Donnarumma; Matheus Nunes, Guehi, Gvardiol, O’Reilly; Bouaddi, Anderson; Allan, Enzo Fernandez, Cherki; Haaland

#1230. Please, Oliver, can we have some more? Celtic boss Martin O'Neill tells Danish midfielder Sorensen it's time to up his game

By JOHN MCGARRY, SCOTTISH CHIEF SPORTS FEATURE WRITER

Published: 13:00 EST, 24 November 2026 | Updated: 13:13 EST, 24 November 2026

Martin O’Neill has told Oliver Sorensen that it’s now time for him to deliver in a Celtic jersey.

The Danish midfielder arrived in Glasgow with a big reputation after coming in on a one-year loan from Parma. But in his seven appearances to date, the 24-year-old has failed to show why the Italian club paid Midtjylland £8.4million for his services a year ago.

With Mika Baur sidelined for up to ten weeks with an ankle injury, Sorensen is likely to be afforded further opportunities to show his worth. But with Alex Oxlade-Chamberlain, Luke McCowan and Joel van den Berg all showing up well in the weekend win over St Mirren, O’Neill has warned that Sorensen needs to do more if he’s to force his way into his side.

‘He has, by his own admission, found it difficult,’ said the Celtic manager.

‘I think that he also arrived late as well, trying to get to know people, trying to get his position, trying to get up to speed with what we do. And whatever we do, I bet you it’ll be something really different to what he was doing at Parma.

‘But now it would be up to him. And, certainly, it will be up to him to try and do something as quickly as possible, whether it’s in the next couple of weeks.

Danish midfielder Oliver Sorensen has been lesser spotted at Celtic this season

‘His strength is picking the ball up deep and running and going with it. I think that Van den Berg can do that as well. But that was the idea with losing (Arne) Engels, we were trying to get a like-for-like replacement.

‘At this minute, he has found it difficult. But he’s willing and he wants to learn.’

Celtic face Torreense on Thursday with the game being played in Leiria as the host club’s normal ground doesn’t meet UEFA stadium requirements.

After losing their first three Europa League games to Ferencvaros, Benfica and Celta Vigo, O’Neill’s men earned a lifeline in the competition when they defeated Besiktas last time out.

With ten points likely to be needed to secure progression to the play-off round, the Celtic manager feels it’s imperative that his side are on the seven-point mark after they take on Omonia on matchday six on December 10.

‘We just want to try and do well,’ he stressed. ‘I said after the Besiktas game that it gives you a chance.

Sorensen struggled along with the rest of his team-mates in a Europa League defeat at Benfica

‘Because nobody’s made it after having lost the first three games. So, the next two matches are vital for us.

‘You’d have to think that we’d need to get four points in the two games to give ourselves a chance.

‘After that you’ve got two left over, a home game (Marseille), which will not be easy. And then the away match (Union Saint-Gilloise).

‘It would be nice to carry it into January and still have a chance.

‘We’ve taken enough criticism for not doing well enough in Europe and rightly so. It’s the aim of the football club, it’s what we’ve always said, and that’s been really disappointing.’

Meanwhile, O’Neill believes Kieran Tierney is rediscovering the form which earned him a £25million move to Arsenal in 2019.

The full-back played the entirety of Scotland’s double-header with North Macedonia and Switzerland and lasted 71 minutes of the win over St Mirren – a game in which he claimed two assists.

O'Neill believes Kieran Tierney is close to the form that earned him a £25m move to Arsenal

Delighted that the player appeared to be putting fitness concerns behind him, O’Neill said: ‘Kieran has done great for me. He’s been brilliant, he really has, and he’s getting fitter too.

‘He will be big for us in Europe again. You look at the Besiktas game. Our winning goal late on came from his shot when he was still getting high up the pitch.

‘Kieran has done so well for us and there are signs that he’s back to the Kieran Tierney who got a move to Arsenal.

‘He defends well, he creates goals and he comes up with some too. I genuinely couldn’t speak highly enough about him. He’s a great lad too, very popular in the dressing room.

‘Kieran can play as a centre-half, there’s no doubt about it. He competes better in the air than I ever thought he could. It was only when I came back to Celtic that I realised that.

‘He will battle in the air and he’s a reliable defender. If we are ever dropping into a back three, then it wouldn’t be a problem for him.’

Manchester United could face a significant financial hurdle in pursuing Everton defender Jarrad Branthwaite, as the centre-back’s potential transfer valuation has now emerged.

The Red Devils have been interested in the 24-year-old for some time, but failed to secure his services in the summer of 2024. However, a fresh move could require a considerably bigger investment than their previous attempts.

According to Football Insider, former Everton scout Bryan King believes the Merseyside club could demand between £ 70 m and £ 80 m to sanction the defender’s departure.

King believes Branthwaite’s performances and Everton’s continued progress make him an attractive proposition for bigger clubs. He also highlighted the defender’s previous injury problems but suggested his recent displays should keep interest in his services strong.

The former scout also questioned Manchester United’s defensive options, suggesting the club needs far more than one new centre-back to improve their backline.

Everton are in a particularly strong negotiating position after securing Branthwaite’s future with a five-year contract in 2025. The Toffees have little reason to entertain a cut-price departure, especially given his importance to their long-term plans.

Want more CaughtOffside coverage? Add us as a preferred source on Google to your favourites list for news you can trust.

United previously had a £ 50 million offer rejected for the English defender in 2024, and their continued admiration could put Everton under pressure if another approach materialises.

Branthwaite reportedly agreed personal terms with the Old Trafford outfit then, although a transfer never came to fruition.

The defender could be an attractive addition for United, given his physical presence, Premier League experience and potential to become a long-term defensive leader.

However, spending up to £ 80 million to secure his signature would be a major investment. Whether United are prepared to meet Everton’s demands remains uncertain, but the Toffees have made their position clear through the valuation suggested by King.

#1228. Taylor shuts down Lazio exit amid Newcastle and Juventus links: ‘I want to help the club return to the Champions League’

Kenneth Taylor has ruled out leaving Lazio in January, insisting he wants to help Gennaro Gattuso’s side return to the Champions League.

According to Il Messaggero, via TuttoMercatoWeb, the Dutch midfielder knows about the interest from Juventus and the Premier League, but has made it clear he isn’t going anywhere.

“It’s all true, my agents have informed me. But I’ve already said I’m not even thinking about leaving in January,” Taylor said. “I want to stay here and help Lazio return to the Champions League.”

The 24-year-old has become one of Serie A’s standout midfielders this season. Tuttosport reported last week that Newcastle have set their sights on him, with Bournemouth and Brentford also after the Dutchman, while Juventus are monitoring his situation.

Lazio have no intention of selling. According to the report, even €40 million might not be enough to convince Claudio Lotito and sporting director Angelo Fabiani to negotiate next summer.

Taylor’s contract already runs until 2030, but he earns only around €1.5m a season, so the club are considering a pay rise to reward his form.

It’s quite a turnaround. Taylor arrived from Ajax in January, and in July Gattuso sent him off the training pitch after a row in pre-season, leaving his future in real doubt. Instead, he has become a key part of Gattuso’s midfield as Lazio sit top of Serie A on 32 points.

He was outstanding again in Saturday’s 3-0 win over Lecce, producing a back-heel that drew comparisons with Rui Costa and completing a record 23 progressive passes.

Published: 14:08 EST, 24 November 2026 | Updated: 14:15 EST, 24 November 2026

Leeds United are in advanced talks with Japan international Ao Tanaka over a new contract.

The 28-year-old midfielder is close to agreeing terms on a deal that will keep him at Elland Road until 2029 with his current contract due to expire in the summer of 2028.

Leeds have lost only 10 games out of the 66 Tanaka has started since joining the club from Fortuna Dusseldorf in 2024. He has had an impressive start to the current campaign, becoming a key figure in Daniel Farke's side, starting in nine of Leeds' 11 Premier League matches. They currently sit seventh in the table.

Leeds have already tied down Ethan Ampadu to a four-year deal while Joe Rodon, Jayden Bogle and Brenden Aaronson all signed new contracts during the summer transfer window.

Talks are also expected to progress over a new deal for Dominic Calvert-Lewin, who has been linked with a move to bitter rivals Manchester United as they look to bolster their striking department.

Discussing Tanaka's form ahead of their emphatic win over Chelsea at the weekend, Farke said: 'It was a big ask for him after spending many years on second-tier level in Germany or here in the Championship.

Ao Tanaka (left) is in advanced talks with Leeds United over signing a new contract until 2029

Leeds are also in talks with striker Dominic Calvert-Lewin over a new deal to stay at Elland Road

'Last season was his first year in the top league. I think he’d shown glimpses of his potential, but he needed to find a bit of consistency. I would agree that he is finding this during the season.

'It was not always a 10 out of 10 performance but I think it's important for a player, once you're mature, that on the weaker days you're still a six or a seven out of 10, and this is what he's doing.

'So perhaps even on the more challenging days, he's at least solid and plays first of all with good confidence, like he always does, but also with a seriousness to be consistent and to work for the team, also against the ball, strong in the duels.

'Still sometimes in decision-making and in front of goal he can be a bit calmer. But overall, I think he's on a really good path to mature more and more. And if you do this, then you become more and more important for us. And we're all happy that he is in such a shape at the moment.'

#1225. Allegri: ‘Napoli must be realistic against Manchester City’

Max Allegri warns Napoli ‘must be realistic’ about their Champions League chances against Manchester City with a decimated squad. ‘We’ve got to be on our toes and play behind them.’

It kicks off at the Etihad in Manchester at 20.00 GMT (21.00 CET).

You can follow all the build-up and action as it happens from this game and Como vs. AEK Athens on the Champions League Liveblog.

The Partenopei have had a dismal run in Europe so far, scraping the 4-3 victory over Bodo/Glimt, but losing the other three to Arsenal, Villarreal and FC Porto.

This is an incredibly tough trip to Manchester, but will be hoping for better than last season, when Giovanni Di Lorenzo was sent off just 21 minutes into a 2-0 defeat.

“This is a wonderful evening against one of the best teams in Europe, they have very technical, physical players,” Allegri told Sky Sport Italia.

“It is going to be very complicated, we must try to be precise, because they will pounce on any mistake and keep pressure on, and when we do make an error, we’ve got to be on our toes.”

The injury crisis keeps getting worse for Napoli, who make the trip without Antonio Vergara, Benoit Badiashile, Alex Meret, Stanislav Lobotka, Giovanni Di Lorenzo, Alisson Santos, Alessandro Buongiorno and suspended Rafa Marin.

This might be a 3-4-2-1 or a 3-5-1-1, depending on Noa Lang, Kevin De Bruyne and Scott McTominay’s positions, but the coach seemed to hint there will be a lot of long balls and crosses.

“When City press us, we must do well to play behind them, then develop it well. If we don’t, then they will intercept loose passes and go on the counter-attack,” replied Allegri when asked about the system.

Napoli have a famously terrible record on English soil in Europe, never winning here, with just four draws from 12 attempts, and the coach seemed almost resigned to his fate before kick-off.

“We are trying to get some players back to fitness, but these injuries and playing every three days, it’s hard to create any momentum, added Allegri.

“As soon as the fixture list came out, I said we had to be realistic. Only an idiot wouldn’t realise Napoli would gamble for qualification in the last three games. That doesn’t mean we came here expecting to lose, but we also need to prepare for another big game this weekend in Serie A.

“I know you like to talk about identity and all these nice words, but we also have to be realistic. We’re against one of the strongest teams in Europe, who dominated for 10 years and then bought even more strong players.

“Football is at times very simple, if you have the best players, you win games. We will try our best, but we’re down to the bare bones, the same players have to keep going because we don’t have the options to rotate, and barely have time to train.

“We are still in the Champions League, regardless what happens tonight, and this weekend will be a very important match for the future of Napoli.”

Napoli will visit relegation strugglers Sassuolo on Saturday.

#1224. Aston Villa's fortunes this season may depend on how quickly Unai Emery can make up his mind on his best XI and tactics as substituting John McGinn backfires in Galatasaray defeat, writes TOM COLLOMOSSE

Published: 15:24 EST, 24 November 2026 | Updated: 16:26 EST, 24 November 2026

Aston Villa made a miserable return to Istanbul as they wasted a wonderful opportunity to put one foot in the last 16 of the Champions League.

In the city that saw them lift the Europa League in May, Villa produced a limp display against a Galatasaray side missing star centre-forward Victor Osimhen. Villa failed to register a shot on target and are now without a win in six games in all competitions.

Substitute Deniz Gul headed the only goal 13 minutes from time as Villa boss Unai Emery cut an angry figure on the touchline and was booked late on. He also appeared to have a tense exchange with midfielder Ross Barkley.

Here Daily Mail Sport's TOM COLLOMOSSE looks at the key moments from another unconvincing Villa display.

Aston Villa left John McGinn out of the starting XI last Saturday and dropped two points in a drab 0-0 draw with Sunderland.

The skipper was back here but three minutes after he was taken off, Villa conceded. Careless defending at a corner allowed Gul to head home, though he took an accidental boot in the face from Nicolas Jackson that required lengthy treatment.

Unai Emery's decision to substitute John McGinn backfired as Aston Villa lost at Galatasaray

Villa conceded three minutes after Emery decided to take off his captain (left) in Istanbul

Deniz Gul scored the only goal of the game with a close-range header on Tuesday evening

With McGinn on the field, Villa would surely have defended the corner better. Jackson's attempted clearance was poor and when the ball looped to Gul, others were too slow to spot the danger.

McGinn and Tyrone Mings are the leaders of this squad and in a period of such change, their role is more important than ever. Though Mings played here, he is no longer a regular starter.

While Emery's wish to protect McGinn is understandable, right now it is a luxury he cannot afford.

Aston Villa (4-2-3-1): Suzuki 6; Harwood-Bellis 6, Lindelof 7, Mings 6, Maatsen 5; Kamara 7 (Buendia 82), J Gomes 6 (Goretzka 66, 6); Alysson 5 (Mbaye 66, 5), McGinn 7 (Barkley 74, 6), Manzambi 5 (Hemmings 74, 6); Jackson 5.

Jackson has nine goals in 15 appearances for Aston Villa - but he has also picked up four yellow cards. Needless bookings proved the forward's downfall during his time at Chelsea and while he has been calmer at Villa, there is still work to do.

During one clash in the first half with Gala defender Davinson Sanchez, Villa boss Unai Emery raced to the edge of his technical area to stop Jackson talking his way into the book. Emery succeeded that time, but not long afterwards, Jackson was punished for a needless tussle with Wilfried Singo.

Jackson plays on the edge. That is a big part of his game. He is also 26 next June and has enough experience to understand when to step into an argument and when to hold back. Emery does not count on Tammy Abraham much these days and Brian Madjo is raw, so he needs Jackson to keep his cool.

The Senegal forward was not the only one to test the patience of referee Daniel Siebert. Joao Gomes was lucky only to be booked for bringing down Yunus Akgun and then grabbing his opponent, while John McGinn was furious that Aleksey Batrakov escaped with a booking for appearing to kick out at the Villa skipper.

Nicolas Jackson's ill-discipline is a concern, with the striker having collected four yellow cards

For most of the last four years, any Villa fan could have written down Emery's first choice XI. Not these days, as Emery still seems to be searching for the ideal formula.

His uncertainty is understandable after losing five key outfield players in the summer but Villa's fortunes this season may depend on how quickly Emery can make up his mind.

Zion Suzuki is the clear first choice in goal and then of the 10 outfield players, how many are lock-ins? Matty Cash and Victor Lindelof in defence. Boubacar Kamara in the middle. John McGinn and - probably - Johan Manzambi in the three-man attacking line, and Nicolas Jackson as centre-forward.

That leaves four spots still up for grabs and not enough of those players are doing enough to convince Emery they deserve the shirt.

#1223. Sleuth finds ‘impossible proteins’ in hundreds of research papers

Thank you for visiting nature.com. You are using a browser version with limited support for CSS. To obtain the best experience, we recommend you use a more up to date browser (or turn off compatibility mode in Internet Explorer). In the meantime, to ensure continued support, we are displaying the site without styles and JavaScript.

Some studies show the expression of proteins such as caspase-3 (pictured) in cell lines that should not be able to produce them. Credit: Dr Mark J. Winter/SPL

A scientific sleuth has identified more than 220 research papers that describe impossible patterns of protein expression in genetically altered cell lines. In these studies, particular proteins show up in imaging experiments, even though the cells do not have the gene necessary to make them.

Journals are now taking action to clean up the literature by retracting or correcting the work, and researchers warn that there are probably many more affected studies.

“This problem will not go away,” says Thierry Soussi, a cancer geneticist at Uppsala University in Sweden, who notes that there are several other examples of the issue in now-retracted papers that were not included in the sleuth’s analysis. “This is only the tip of a gigantic iceberg.”

Cell lines are groups of cells derived from a single origin cell and cultured for use in experiments. Some cancer cell lines have been genetically modified with mutations and deletions — often to remove genes that usually control cell division. This means that the cultures continually divide and grow, giving researchers the chance to study tumour progression and test potential treatments.

The MCF-7 cell line is one of these. It lacks the gene for caspase-3 protein, which is involved in cell death. In 2009, researchers warned1 that some studies that report working with MCF-7 have mysteriously observed caspase-3 expression in western blots, an imaging technique that identifies proteins on the basis of their molecular weight.

Sleuth identifies dozens of studies that used the wrong antibody

Sleuth identifies dozens of studies that used the wrong antibody

In the most recent analysis, published as a preprint on 21 October to the data repository Zenodo2, Sholto David, a sleuth based in Arbroath, UK, finds that this problem persists and extends to other cell lines.

David compiled a list of 20 commonly used cell lines with genetic mutations or deletions that leave cells unable to express specific proteins. He then scoured the literature using Google text and image searches to identify examples of western-blot images that unexpectedly identify these proteins. He also searched a collection of 140,000 articles that he had previously downloaded and screened for image-integrity issues and other problems, most of which were biomedicine papers.

He found 230 reports of phantom proteins across 221 papers published since 2004. The most common errors were observations of caspase-3 expression in the MCF-7 cell line, affecting 49 papers; expression of the cell-death protein BAX in the Jurkat cell line in 47 papers; and expression of the signalling protein STAT3 in the PC-3 cell line in 35 papers.

David suggests several explanations for these impossible protein-expression patterns. They might be the result of honest errors: researchers could have misidentified the cell lines or contaminated them with others. Or the antibodies used to identify proteins in the western-blot experiments could have been non-specific and bound to another protein with the same molecular weight. In fact, David says that he stumbled across the anomalous proteins while working on a project that flagged hundreds of studies that used the wrong antibodies in experiments.

Another possibility is that some of the papers are the product of paper mills, companies that fabricate and sell scientific manuscripts. David says that some papers in the cache contain the hallmarks of being produced by such outfits, including duplicated images or text templates that are similar to other papers. The proportion of the papers that fall into this category is not clear, he says.

Nature has contacted several authors of papers containing anomalies to ask for comment, but none responded.

Science sleuths raise concerns about scores of bioengineering papers

Bruno Fernandes has put discussions over a new Manchester United contract on hold, insisting the club’s immediate priority should be winning football matches rather than deciding his future.

The United captain’s situation has attracted considerable attention after two contract proposals were reportedly rejected, but his latest comments provide important context.

Fernandes is not suggesting his Old Trafford career is over. Instead, he believes negotiations should wait while Mauricio Pochettino attempts to drag United away from the wrong end of the Premier League table.

As reported by Fabrizio Romano, Fernandes has confirmed that contract discussions have stopped for the time being.

“Contract talks have stopped for us to start winning games… and then we can talk about contract”.

“It’s not important now. It’s my future, I haven’t got much left in my contract, but we will have time to speak about that”.

United are not completely exposed despite the uncertainty. Fernandes’ existing agreement expires next summer, but the club hold an option to extend it until 2028.

A CaughtOffside report also highlights that United have offered their captain a new contract, while Fernandes has dismissed suggestions that his stance is motivated by demands for more money or additional years.

This feels less like Fernandes rejecting Man United and more like the captain challenging the club to give him a reason to commit.

At 32, his next contract could determine where he spends the final years of his career at the highest level. Signing another long-term agreement while United are struggling near the bottom of the table would require enormous faith in the latest rebuild.

Pochettino therefore has an important role.

Improved results, smart January recruitment and evidence of a clear footballing direction could do more to convince Fernandes than simply increasing his salary.

United should activate their extension if necessary, protecting themselves from losing such a valuable player cheaply.

But the long-term solution is not contractual leverage. It is proving to Fernandes that Old Trafford remains the right place to compete for major trophies.

His message is ultimately straightforward: fix the football first, and discuss the future afterwards.

It was a chastening afternoon for the champions who last won at Welford Road in January 2023.

Phil Dowson, Saints’ director of rugby, felt his side were in the contest at the interval but bemoaned the fact that they were unable to handle Leicester’s second-half power surge.

“It was a scrap. The conditions were going to dictate that. And they had some set-piece dominance which hurt us,” he said.

“That gave them a ton of energy and we didn’t seem able to respond, which was probably the most disappointing thing.

“In the second half we didn’t seem to have that same buzz about us.”

Dowson was reluctant to blame the tunnel flare-up for the turnaround.

“The fracas at the end of the half was just one of those things that happens in a derby – that happens every derby. I don’t think that’s necessarily something that triggered anything,” he said.

“It’s not as if anyone got filled in. Well, you just can’t anymore, can you? These games are going to be hostile and in the current game you can’t throw anything. It’s just push and shove and talk c--p, so I don’t think that had any impact.”

Northampton stand-off Fin Smith was withdrawn late on with a dead leg but he is expected to join up with the England squad for training on Monday.

Leicester were buoyed in the week by re-signing Jack van Poortfliet, who extended his contract with his boyhood club.

I grew up supporting Leicester, it’s always been my club,” said the England scrum half. This place feels like home in my rugby life. The club is in a really good position, I think we have a great group of lads and great coaches.

I love playing rugby here, I have my best mates here and I believe that we’ve got a group of lads that we can do great things with. I want to be in a place that I love playing for and I believe can win trophies.”

It’s a big day for Alex Coles, who celebrates his milestone 150th cap today.

The 27-year-old lock follows Fraser Dingwall, Rory Hutchinson and Alex Mitchell to become the fourth member of Saints’ current squad to reach 150 appearances for his boyhood club, eight years after making his debut in 2018.

Coles marks one of nine changes to Saints’ side for the Derby Day clash, with Emmanuel Iyogun, Curtis Langdon, Ed Prowse, Tom Pearson and Henry Pollock the other names coming into the forward pack.

Cleopas Kundiona retains his place in the front row while milestone man Coles joins Prowse in the second row against Tigers.

Josh Kemeny, with the 27-year-old continues at blindside flanker while Tom Pearson is set to make his first Prem appearance of the season.

Northampton Saints: J Pater; T Freeman, R Hutchinson, F Dingwall, G Hendy; F Smith, A Mitchell, E Iyogun, C Langdon, C Kundiona, A Coles, E Prowse, J Kemeny, T Pearson, H Pollock.

Replacements: R Smith, D Fischetti, I Neculai, JJ Van Der Mescht, T Lockett, C Chick, A McParland, O Sleightholme.

Parling has made five changes from the side that endured a 41-17 defeat to Pau.

Solomone Kata returns from injury to start at inside centre, with Gabriel Hamer-Webb and Jack van Poortvliet also coming into the backline to replace Ollie Hassell-Collins and Tom Whiteley respectively.

In the pack, Joe Heyes joins Archie van der Flier and Jamie Blamire who retain their places in the front row, while the second row make up of Cameron Henderson and Ollie Chessum remains unchanged.

Aaron Wainwright comes back into the starting lineup in the back row, with Finn Carnduff moving to openside flanker, with Olly Cracknell going at No 8.

Leicester: F Steward; A Radwan, W Wand, S Kata; G Hamer-Webb; B Searle, J van Poortvliet; A van der Flier, J Blamire, J Heyes, C Henderson, O Chessum, A Wainwright, F Carnduff, O Cracknell.

Replacements:  R Asiata, T Haffar, W Hurd, J Thompson, J Moro, T Whiteley, O Bailey, G Pearson.

Hello and welcome to our live coverage of Leicester Tigers v Northampton Saints.

The Prem’s derby weekend continues today at Mattioli Woods Welford Road, where Geoff Parling’s side go head-to-head in with their East Midlands rivals.

Both Leicester and Northampton have two wins from the opening three rounds of the season and with both sides involved in a number of high-scoring encounters already in the new campaign, we could be in for a real treat.

Tigers started the season with a 38-40 loss at home to Saracens, but bounced back quickly with wins over Gloucester and Newcastle Red Bulls. They will be itching to right a few wrongs after suffering a chastening Champions Cup defeat in Pau last week.

Northampton, meanwhile, have notched up wins over Newcastle Red Bulls and Bath either side of loss to Bristol Bears.

A win today for Saints would be their first on the road since defeating Exeter Chiefs at Sandy Park in April.

“It (the East Midlands derby) means a lot to everyone, we know it will be a great atmosphere at Mattioli Woods Welford Road,” said Parling.

“I don’t think with this sort of game either team has to build it up too much emotionally because that just comes, so I think it’s actually about being really really calm in the moment.”

“Hopefully we can put the best of ourselves out there and I’m sure Saints will be able to do exactly the same.”

Saints are without a victory in Leicester since January 2023, when a single point decided the 18-19 result.

Since then, the last five meetings between the sides have been won by the hosts on the day – with Saints last taking home the bragging rights when a Tom Litchfield hat-trick helped Northampton to a 45-31 win on home soil in last season’s league play-off.

Kick-off gets underway at 3.05pm. Stay with us here for all the latest updates.

#1219. Alejandro Garnacho's nightmare Aston Villa loan continues: Struggling star is left at home as Unai Emery picks TWO goalkeepers on bench for Galatasaray defeat before sending warning to ex-Man United winger

Published: 17:00 EST, 24 November 2026 | Updated: 17:05 EST, 24 November 2026

Alejandro Garnacho's future at Aston Villa was plunged into further doubt on Tuesday as he was overlooked for their defeat at Galatasaray.

The Argentine joined on loan from Chelsea last summer with a £43million obligation to buy, triggered when certain targets were hit.

Yet Garnacho has yet to start for Villa and was not even on the bench in Istanbul, even though two goalkeepers were named.

Asked whether Garnacho was fit for this match, Villa boss Unai Emery said: 'Today I think the best players to play with us, to be with us, were here.'

Daily Mail Sport has reported regularly this season that Garnacho may not see out his loan spell and now that looks increasingly likely to be the case.

There is not thought to be a break clause in the loan but if Chelsea and Villa agreed to cancel it, that would allow Garnacho to go elsewhere in January.

Alejandro Garnacho was not in the Aston Villa squad for their defeat at Galatasaray on Tuesday

Villa boss Unai Emery chose to include two goalkeepers on his bench instead of picking of him

Villa had a similar situation with Harvey Elliott. The midfielder joined on loan from Liverpool in summer 2025 but barely played.

Emery decided quickly that he did not want to sign Elliott permanently and could not risk triggering the appearance clause that would have seen him join Villa for £35m.

Villa are now without a win in six and Emery admitted: 'The next challenge against PSG at home will be huge. If we can recover the three points we lost today maybe we still have a chance to reach the top eight but we are not favourites.'

Emery also bemoaned the home side's time-wasting tactics after Deniz Gul headed them into a 77th-minute lead.

He said: 'I am not blaming the referee but he was unfair with us by adding only five minutes. After they scored it was impossible to play.'

Manchester United have reportedly made Bournemouth left-back Adrien Truffert their “dream target” for the January transfer window as Mauricio Pochettino looks to strengthen a struggling squad.

United’s disastrous start to the season has increased the urgency around their winter plans.

Sitting 19th in the Premier League following a 4-0 defeat to Liverpool in Pochettino’s first match in charge, the Red Devils desperately need reinforcements capable of making an immediate difference.

Truffert now appears to have moved right to the top of their defensive shopping list.

According to GIVEMESPORT, ManUnited have identified Truffert as their “dream target” for January.

The France international has been linked with United for several months, but the latest report suggests their interest has become significantly more serious following Pochettino’s arrival.

United had previously considered Newcastle United’s Lewis Hall as a leading option at left-back. However, Newcastle are determined to resist January interest in the England international, potentially making Truffert the more realistic target.

Bournemouth will not make negotiations easy either. A FootballTransfers report claimed the Cherries value Truffert at around £60million and would prefer not to sell him midway through the season.

There is plenty to like about this potential signing.

Truffert is Premier League proven, athletic and comfortable contributing at both ends of the pitch.

At 25, he is also entering his prime rather than arriving as another expensive prospect who needs several seasons to develop.

United clearly need greater reliability at left-back, particularly given Luke Shaw’s recurring fitness problems. The concern is the price.

Spending around £60m on a full-back in January would consume a significant portion of United’s available budget when Pochettino also needs improvements elsewhere.

However, their league position changes the calculation. United cannot afford to treat January as a window simply for long-term planning.

If Pochettino believes Truffert can immediately improve the defence and become his long-term first-choice left-back, United should seriously explore the deal.

The challenge will be convincing Bournemouth to sell one of their most important players halfway through a difficult season without paying an enormous January premium.

#1217. Gasperini: ‘A great moment for Roma to face the best’ ahead of PSG test

Gian Piero Gasperini says Roma’s trip to Paris Saint-Germain is “a great moment” to test themselves against the best, and admits the Lisbon defeat with Atalanta still leaves a bitter taste.

With quotes via TuttoMercatoWeb, the Roma coach was speaking at his pre-match press conference at the Parc des Princes, alongside Paulo Dybala, ahead of Wednesday’s Champions League clash. Kick-off is at 21:00 CET [20:00 GMT].

“It’s definitely a very, very good moment for us to be able to play this game against the strongest team,” Gasperini said. “What we’re thinking about most at the moment is putting in a high-level performance.

“It’s clear we have to measure ourselves against this team. It’s the first time we’ve faced them with Roma, so we’ll have to understand straight away on the pitch what their level is. It’s certainly very high, and we need to see how much we can counter their technique and their speed. Our aim is to reduce their effectiveness a little so that we can also play our own game.”

Roma go to Paris with four points from four games after dramatic defeats to Real Madrid and Manchester United. PSG, the holders, have won all four of theirs.

Gasperini insisted those losses shouldn’t affect his side’s confidence.

“This is what the Champions League is like. It’s the most important competition in the world, with the highest level,” he said. “You can put in very good performances, like we did against Real and Manchester, but then there are key moments, and the best players in the world are on the pitch and can decide games.

“We have to focus on producing that type of performance, because it gives you confidence, makes you grow and carries over into the league.”

This is not Gasperini’s first big night against PSG. In the 2020 quarter-final in Lisbon, his Atalanta side were leading going into the final minutes, but lost 2-1 to two late goals.

“That’s a game that’s still a bit hard to swallow, because of the ending,” he admitted. “We were down to 10 men in the final minutes because of Freuler’s injury and had no substitutions left. PSG brought on Mbappé, and he was decisive. But it’s still one of the highest moments in Atalanta’s history.

“This is a different type of game, because PSG are different. They’re much more of a team now, and that’s thanks to Luis Enrique. Roma are coming into this competition after several years away, which is different for us. It’s a league-phase game, and for us it’s a measure of what we’re doing.”

This was hardly “the Battle of the Bridge”, but Chelsea blew up during a ridiculous 10-minute spell towards the end of a game in which Tottenham had bossed possession but not looked like scoring.

Palmer was lucky to stay on the pitch in the 70th minute, when he shoved his pelvis into the face of Mateus Fernandes after the Tottenham midfielder had stopped him racing through with a foul and a handball.

Hello and welcome to our live coverage of this mouthwatering Premier League game between Chelsea and Tottenham at Stamford Bridge.

Chelsea secured a hard-fought 2-0 away win at Everton last weekend thanks to Pedro Neto’s double, while Tottenham earned their first Premier League victory of the season on Monday, beating Frank Lampard’s Coventry City 3-1 at home.

It’s Xabi Alonso’s first taste of the bitter rivalry and has hyped up the atmosphere ahead of the clash. “We are expecting a good atmosphere,” he said. “Electric, with good energy, knowing that in a derby this passion is really in the air in the stadium.

“We need that connection with the crowd in good moments. There will be tough moments, but we need to pull together and play our game. For me, it’s fundamental that we play our game on the pitch.

“The players, they do their best, but when the crowd is playing the game, is living it, that’s the good thing about the Premier League. I think the crowd plays the game as well. It’s not that they just watch the game.”

Chelsea will be without Emiliano Martinez, who fractured his jaw against Everton, with Mike Penders poised to start. Reece James, Pep Chavarria and Emmanuel Emegha are also ruled out.

As for Tottenham, Rodrigo Bentancur remains suspended, while Destiny Udogie, Lucas Bergvall, Wilson Odobert and Xavi Simons are unavailable. James Maddison and Dejan Kulusevski enjoyed happy returns to the first team against Coventry following lengthy injuries and could feature here.

It’s safe to say that the statistics aren’t on Spurs’ side. Roberto De Zerbi will be well aware of Tottenham’s dismal record at Stamford Bridge, where Spurs have won just once in 41 across all competitions. Tottenham have also only beaten once in their 15 previous Premier League meetings – a 2-0 victory over Graham Potter’s Chelsea in 2023.

Games between these bitter rivals always carry a feistiness and an added edge. Drama is guaranteed. Kick-off is at 17:30, with team news coming shortly.

Florian Wirtz has credited Andoni Iraola with helping him rediscover his best football at Liverpool after emerging from a difficult period to become one of the Reds’ most influential attacking players.

The German international struggled to consistently reproduce his Bayer Leverkusen form following his £116million move to Anfield in 2025.

However, the picture now looks very different, with Wirtz enjoying an impressive run under Iraola and appearing increasingly comfortable with English football.

Speaking ahead of Liverpool’s Champions League clash with Club Brugge, Wirtz told Liverpool’s official website that Iraola’s confidence has played a major role in his resurgence.

“I’m really enjoying playing under Iraola. He’s a really good coach and has shown that his whole career as a manager”.

“He is bringing me back in a place where I was maybe two years ago where I played really good football, I can feel that he gives me the confidence and I’m really happy about that”.

Wirtz scored and assisted in Liverpool’s emphatic 4-0 victory over Manchester United on Sunday, having also registered a goal and assist against Crystal Palace before the international break.

A CaughtOffside report highlighted just how dominant he was against United. Wirtz created 10 chances from open play, reportedly the highest total by a Premier League player in a single match since David Silva recorded 11 in 2015.

This is exactly what Liverpool supporters expected when Wirtz arrived from Leverkusen.

His talent was never really the issue. Adapting to the Premier League, finding his best position and playing with confidence were bigger obstacles. Iraola appears to have addressed all three.

Wirtz is now operating with greater freedom and combining effectively with Liverpool’s other attacking players, while his improved physical condition and greater familiarity with English football are also helping.

Perhaps most importantly, Iraola trusted him when performances were not producing enough end product.

Liverpool invested heavily because they believed Wirtz could become the creative centrepiece of their attack. They are now beginning to see that player.

If this trajectory continues, Iraola’s biggest achievement at Liverpool may not simply be improving results, it could be turning Wirtz into the Premier League superstar the club always believed they were signing.

In the meantime, to ensure continued support, we are displaying the site without styles and JavaScript.

In this plot of the Riemann ζ function on the complex plane, every point represents a complex number, with the real part plotted on the horizontal axis (from −10 to 10) and the imaginary part on the vertical axis (also from −10 to 10). The colours represent the output of the function, with the junctions where the hues converge around a point showing some of the all-important zeroes.Credit: Empetrisor via Wikimedia Commons (CC BY-SA 4.0)

In a year that has seen artificial intelligence reach one spectacular mathematical breakthrough after another, Anthropic has now claimed the top prize of them all: a full proof of the Riemann hypothesis, the statement that many mathematicians consider the most important open problem in the field. But on the same day as the Anthropic claim, a separate study claiming to have proven the Riemann also emerged — and this one is entirely human written.

The Anthropic announcement came on 20 November from Levent Alpöge, a mathematician at the San Francisco, California, company. “I believe I have, working with Claude, discovered a proof of the Riemann Hypothesis,” Alpöge wrote, referring to Anthropic’s large language model (LLM).

AI is ‘the end of mathematics as we know it’ — where does the field go next?

AI is ‘the end of mathematics as we know it’ — where does the field go next?

“If this fully checks out, it is clearly a historic milestone in mathematics,” says number theorist James Maynard, a winner of the Fields Medal — mathematics’ most prestigious prize — at the University of Oxford, UK.

Hours later, Ravi Vakil, a mathematician at Stanford University in California, posted a rival preprint to Alpöge’s online, in what Vakil called a “hurried announcement” of a proof that “is all human, with no AI”. The preprint was written by Alessandro Maria Masullo, a mathematician who received his PhD at Stanford in 2020 under the supervision of number theorist Brian Conrad. “The hope was to have Brian work with Alessandro for a year to polish the writing and then announce it after running it by enough people,” Vakil wrote. “Now it seems best to put out the current draft.”

The confirmation of either or both solutions would be a spectacular bicentenary present for Bernhard Riemann, the German mathematician who was born 200 years ago this September and who formulated the problem, which addresses the distribution of prime numbers, in the mid-1800s.

The Riemann hypothesis is one of the seven Millennium Prize Problems selected by the Clay Mathematics Institute, which has its scientific headquarters in Oxford, UK, at the turn of the twenty-first century. The institute offers a US$1 million prize to anyone who devises a solution to one of the problems, which are considered some of the most challenging in the field. Mathematicians using AI tools announced earlier this year that they had solved another Millennium problem, related to the Navier-Stokes equation.

The problem has to do with the ‘Riemann ζ function’ (ζ is the Greek letter zeta), which encodes the randomness properties of the prime numbers. Riemann discovered that the distribution of primes is encoded in the ζ function’s ‘zeroes’. These are points, denoted by z, on a plane satisfying the equation ζ(z) = 0.

Riemann conjectured that apart from some obvious but uninteresting cases, all such solutions had to lie on a certain vertical line in the plane. If this were true, he showed, it would imply that prime numbers are scattered among all whole numbers in a way that is essentially as random as it could be.

The Riemann hypothesis has been a lodestar for generations of mathematicians. Credit: James Brittain/Getty

Alpöge’s four-page document includes a sketch of the proof. But Andrew Granville, a number theorist at the University of Montreal in Canada, says that Alpöge should have taken the time to prepare a clearer write-up before making the announcement, which came just days after Anthropic’s initial public offering (IPO). The IPO initially valued the company at US$1.5 trillion, but the company’s valuation dropped on 19 November.

“What he released is garbled,” Granville says of Alpöge’s document. Granville cites the downturn in the company’s stock value as the reason for the timing of the proof’s release.

“There is an obvious cynical view, to do with the timing, but it is false,” Alpöge wrote in the document.

Anthropic did not respond immediately to Nature’s request for comment.

Tristan Buckmaster, a mathematician at New York University who collaborated with Alpöge on a separate project regarding the Navier-Stokes equation, says that Alpöge deserves a lot of credit for developing techniques to produce mathematical results using LLMs. “Levent himself built this amazing set-up to do math.” He adds that Alpöge, who is himself a number theorist on leave from Harvard University in Cambridge, Massachusetts, has been working relentlessly for months on this and other problems, hardly ever getting any sleep.

‘The job description is changing’: mathematician Terence Tao on the rise of AI

‘The job description is changing’: mathematician Terence Tao on the rise of AI

“I suspect that the proof will turn out to be correct,” Maynard says of the Alpöge announcement, even though it is now in the form of incomprehensible code in the Lean programming language.

#1213. Napoli director Manna on McTominay chat, De Bruyne tension and Zirkzee report

Napoli director of sport Giovanni Manna confirms a meeting with Scott McTominay’s agent, insists Kevin De Bruyne ‘is our player’ and shrugs off Joshua Zirkzee rumours ahead of the Manchester City match.

It kicks off at the Etihad in Manchester at 20.00 GMT (21.00 CET).

You can follow all the build-up and action as it happens from this game and Como vs. AEK Athens on the Champions League Liveblog.

This is a familiar city to Manna, who has come to Manchester several times in recent years to secure reinforcements for the club, including De Bruyne as a free agent in the summer of 2025.

“I came to Manchester to pick up McTominay first, and then De Bruyne,” Manna told Sky Sport Italia.

“De Bruyne experiences the build-up to the game the same way, he was here last year too. I think he feels pride to be here after everything he achieved.”

De Bruyne tried to give a little more clarity on his future after his wife implied they might want a return to the Netherlands for PSV Eindhoven.

“Kevin De Bruyne is our player, he is under contract to the end of the season, and there is an option to extend. You know what the transfer market is like, all it takes is a comment to spiral out of control. It’s early days, anything could happen, we’re very calm and look to the future with a relaxed attitude,” added the Napoli director.

“This evening’s match might seem prohibitive, and maybe it is, but we have to give our best and then focus on Serie A from the weekend.”

There has been a lot of speculation over McTominay’s future and the negotiations to extend his contract, with reports Manna met the Scotland international’s agent in the team hotel while they were in town for the match against Manchester City.

“We just had a coffee, because his agent is from here. We had a chat about many things, not just football.”

It is also suggested that Manna and Napoli will swing back round here in January for Manchester United striker Joshua Zirkzee.

“There are many talented players in Manchester, both for United and City, so let’s focus on tonight’s game because we really need the points.”

#1212. Bruno Fernandes opens door to Sporting return amid doubts over Man United future as captain insists 'now is not the time' to discuss new contract

Published: 17:50 EST, 24 November 2026 | Updated: 17:54 EST, 24 November 2026

Bruno Fernandes has left the door open for a return to Sporting Lisbon amid increasing uncertainty over his future at Manchester United.

Fernandes was a fans’ favourite at Sporting before joining United in January 2020 in a deal worth up to £68million.

The United captain has become equally popular at Old Trafford, but returned to Lisbon on Tuesday night with a question mark hanging over his next move after talks over a new contract stalled.

Fernandes’ current deal is due to run out at the end of June – and he will be able to speak to foreign clubs from January 1 – although United are expected to trigger an automatic 12-month extension to prevent him from leaving as a free agent in the summer.

Asked if he would consider a move back to the Jose Alvalade Stadium, where United meet Sporting in the Champions League on Wednesday night, Fernandes said: ‘I will never close the door to Sporting. It will always be a club with a special place in my heart.

‘Sporting was the first club that believed in my potential. I’ve always felt here from the fans – regardless of what may have happened – all the love and kindness from them, and that was essential to make me grow as a player.’

Bruno Fernandes has rejected two offers of a new contract to extend his stay at Man United

On his future at Old Trafford, Fernandes insisted that he wants to focus on turning United’s season around after they slipped into the relegation zone and replaced head coach Michael Carrick with Mauricio Pochettino.

‘We have time to speak about that,’ said Fernandes. ‘I know it's my future and I probably shouldn't look that way because I haven't got long left, but I'm more worried about results.

‘Contract talks have stopped for us to start winning games, and then we can talk about a contract. Now is not the moment.’

#1211. Most expensive goal in Liverpool history gives Iraola era lift-off

A quick sprint, a well-placed pass and an instinctive finish. Bradley Barcola and Alexander Isak will have done this dozens of times in training but here, on a squally Sunday afternoon, this combination secured a little piece of history.

Anfield has witnessed plenty of significant goals down the years but never had this crowd seen one that cost £248m to make. Liverpool invested a near quarter-billion pounds on Barcola and Isak for bigger occasions than a tussle with Brighton and Hove Albion, but this rapid interchange felt like a significant moment.

Liverpool are a work in progress under Andoni Iraola but with each minute of each game you can see signs of things knitting together, and if Barcola and Isak are finding harmony, with Florian Wirtz in behind, then, perhaps, this journey will start to accelerate.

This was an important afternoon for Liverpool’s head coach, a difficult assignment against high-flying, well-respected opponents in Brighton, who arrived on Merseyside having won their last four Premier League fixtures with a combined aggregate of 15-0, including a 3-0 thumping of reigning champions Arsenal.

But Liverpool rose impressively to the challenge and there are grounds for saying this was the most significant success to date for Iraola, whose team defended relentlessly to preserve a clean sheet. They are up to fourth now after this 2-0 success and deserve their position.

“I’m very happy,” Iraola said. “We faced a very good opponent, similar to Villarreal [in the Champions League]. It’s difficult to defend them a lot of times and it was key how we started. We needed to be aggressive, recover balls, win our duels, be dangerous in transitions: I think we’ve done it.”

And how. Iraola was able to march towards the Kop at the end, to clap the supporters and acknowledge only Liverpool’s fifth (and his first) Premier League win at Anfield in 2026, and it was evident he had a spring in his step from what he had seen.

Whether the game would have flowed in the direction it did had Brighton taken the lead can only be speculated but what a glorious chance they wasted for us to find out: in the 13th minute, five swift, one-touch passes bamboozled Liverpool’s defence and created space for Yasin Ayari.

With the goal at his mercy, Ayari could have made things exceptionally uncomfortable but he leant back and blazed over. He clasped his face and grimaced, knowing what had gone begging in front of the Kop; four minutes later, his misery was exacerbated.

"He's GOT to hit the target!" Yasin Ayari missed a golden chance to put Brighton ahead against Liverpool 🫣 https://t.co/Qz7G3sXCpP

Liverpool’s lead was secured with an element of good fortune but, equally, the tenacity of Ronald Araújo and Wirtz was instrumental in pressing Brighton back to the point that they were panicking; Wirtz’s shot, deflected off Pascal Gross past Bart Verbruggen, compounded it all.

“I think everyone in the stadium – and you as well – felt there was a missed opportunity for us,” groaned Fabian Hürzeler, the visitors’ head coach. “It’s not only after the goal or the goals they scored. Before they scored, we had two big chances. I think it was just the difference that they scored and we didn’t score.”

It would be wrong to say Wirtz was doing cartwheels – perhaps he knew immediately he would not get the goal – but it was an important moment for him and you could feel the sense of goodwill towards him from team-mates and supporters alike.

Florian Wirtz's deflected shot has put Liverpool ahead minutes after Brighton had a great chance of their own ⚽️ https://t.co/b6mRvl2rSR

Remarkably, this was the first time Liverpool had scored in the first half at Anfield in a Premier League fixture since May 9 and, with that momentum, it led to one of those periods when they started attacking in waves and carried the crowd with them.

What they needed was a second goal to arrive quite quickly and that is what happened when Barcola won possession, scuttled forward and played a perfectly weighted bobbling ball into Isak’s path; the Swede did the rest, calmly finishing from eight yards.

Everything with Isak feels to be going under the radar at the moment, but that is six goals in six Premier League appearances. He is starting to show the consistency and killer instinct that everyone felt he would. Iraola will be hoping it continues for the foreseeable future.

Alexander Isak scores to double Liverpool's lead at Anfield! 💥 https://t.co/oYs2jnHZEb

“The performance was really good,” said Isak, the quiet assassin. “We were really solid against a really good team. The first half is what we really want to be about. It was about intensity, winning balls and countering.”

Brighton, as much as Hürzeler protested, could not properly recover, though this is no criticism. They remain committed to attack, they struck the frame of the goal when Ayari tried to punish an Alisson Becker mistake and the desire to keep pushing ensured Liverpool could never relax.

What Liverpool had going for them this time, however, was an intensity to preserve a clean sheet and nobody embodied the indefatigability more than Araújo, the Uruguay international whose loan from Barcelona is looking an increasingly shrewd piece of business.

Two moments stood out: one thunderous tackle on substitute Malick Yalcouyé in front of the Main Stand that had the locals roaring their approval, another in the first half when he was on the floor but still managed to head away to thwart Maxim De Cuyper.

They remember those moments as much as the stardust that Barcola and Isak provide. Put it all together and it might just be a launchpad for Iraola.

Liverpool are on a three-game winning run in all competitions, and came from two goals behind in their previous outing in the Champions League on Tuesday, earning an enthralling 4-3 victory over Villarreal. Last weekend, Andoni Iraola’s men also initially fell behind against Brentford in the Premier League, but netted two second-half goals through Daniel Munoz and Alexander Isak to win 2-1 as their opponents finished with nine men.

In his programme notes, Liverpool boss Iraola was excited about the prospect of a second game in a week at home. “As someone who believes every single opportunity we have to play a game at this stadium and in front of our supporters is a privilege, I also feel very passionately that this is a period that we should continue to embrace,” he said.

“It is also a spell in which we will carry on being tested because the quality of the opposition dictates that there is no chance of anything else. Villarreal pushed us all the way in midweek and everything about the way Brighton have played so far this season tells us that it would be foolish to expect anything but the same today.”

Brighton have emerged as one of the surprise packages of the Premier League season thanks to their blistering start. Fabian Hurzeler’s side sit third in the table, having scored a whopping 23 goals in their opening seven games, while conceding just five. On Thursday, Brighton were unexpectedly held to a 0-0 draw by Czech outfit Jablonec, ending a run of six straight victories in all competitions. Nevertheless, they’re unbeaten since their 4-3 league loss to Chelsea back on August 30.

Defender Ferdi Kadioglu believes his team’s energy and fitness has played a huge role in their eye-catching form. “If you want to play how we play, you have to be very fit,” he said. “We were already fit last season, but I think it’s more that now everyone really understands what we need to do to win matches. That’s really clear this season, and everyone is doing it. Everyone is really focused on their task and doing it very well so far.”

Kick-off is at 14:00, with team news following shortly.

Ayden Heaven is reportedly open to leaving Manchester United on loan in January as the highly-rated defender searches for the regular football needed to continue his development.

The 20-year-old has struggled for consistent minutes during a turbulent period at Old Trafford and now finds himself working under his third manager since arriving from Arsenal in February 2025.

With Mauricio Pochettino tasked with dragging United out of the Premier League relegation zone, Heaven appears concerned that experience will be prioritised over potential during the coming months.

According to BBC Sport, Heaven is open to a January loan after becoming concerned about his game time and what United’s current situation could mean for his development.Those concerns were highlighted during Sunday’s 4-0 defeat to Liverpool.

Heaven remained an unused substitute even after Leny Yoro was sent off early in the game, with Pochettino instead turning to experienced defender Harry Maguire.

The former Arsenal youngster has made 32 senior appearances since moving to Old Trafford, but only two of his Premier League appearances this season have been starts.

Heaven remains contracted until 2029, with United also holding an option for another year. Fulham and Barcelona, who both showed interest before his move from Arsenal, are reportedly still admirers.

Allowing Heaven to leave temporarily could be the sensible solution.

United clearly rate his long-term potential, but their current circumstances make developing a young centre-back particularly difficult. Pochettino needs immediate results and understandably may favour experienced defenders while fighting relegation.

United are considering defensive reinforcements, with The Sun reporting that Fulham’s Calvin Bassey is among the centre-backs on their radar, although Fulham are attempting to secure him to a new contract and do not want a January sale.

Another arrival would push Heaven further down the hierarchy.

Selling him permanently, however, would feel unnecessarily short-sighted.

Heaven is only 20 and has already demonstrated enough potential to suggest he could eventually become an important United defender.

A carefully chosen loan, ideally somewhere offering regular top-level football, would allow him to develop away from the pressure surrounding Old Trafford before returning in the summer ready to compete for Pochettino’s trust.

Published: 18:12 EST, 24 November 2026 | Updated: 18:24 EST, 24 November 2026

Florian Wirtz has thanked Liverpool boss Andoni Iraola for sparking his resurgence and insists he never stopped believing in himself.

The German arrived with a big reputation when he completed a £116million move from Bayer Leverkusen but has been a constant punchbag for critics after failing to reach the heights that saw him win the Bundesliga title as the league’s star man.

Wirtz, though, has been much improved this year and put in his best performance for the Reds on Sunday in the 4-0 thumping of Manchester United And he insists Iraola – and old Anfield boss Jurgen Klopp – are the reason.

‘I am really enjoying playing under him,’ said Wirtz on Iraola, who replaced Arne Slot in the summer. ‘He is a really good coach. He has shown that his whole career as a manager.

‘He is bringing me back to the place where I was maybe two years ago where I played really good football.

‘I can feel that he gives me confidence and I am really happy about that. I am just trying to give him back what he gives me. I am really happy with that.’

Florian Wirtz has opened up on talking to ex-Liverpool boss Jurgen Klopp after finally hitting form for Liverpool

Wirtz won man of the match in Liverpool's 4-0 thrashing of Manchester United on Sunday

Wirtz has also had the added influence of Klopp, now Germany boss, in recent months. He said: ‘We always speak about Liverpool when we have the time to do so. He had a great time here. He is the coach who stayed here the most of his career.

‘He just tells me all the time that he loved his time here, the people love him here, he tries to give me some advice to get successful over here because he has shown how it is done.

'He knows a lot about this club, a lot of people here, he can give me some good advice.’

Wirtz added: ‘It's not about the people who talk about me. It's the goals I set myself and the performances I want to show for myself.

#1207. Genoa defender Ostigard spends night in hospital with high fever

Genoa defender Leo Ostigard spent Monday night in hospital after suffering a sudden high fever, although tests have since ruled out anything serious.

According to ANSA, the Norway international was taken to Genoa’s San Martino Hospital in the early hours, after the fever came with a severe headache.

He was examined by infectious disease specialist Professor Matteo Bassetti and his team. The routine diagnostic tests came back reassuring and ruled out any significant medical problems. Ostigard will nonetheless remain under observation at the hospital for the rest of today.

The scare came just a day after one of his best performances of the season. Ostigard was among Genoa’s standout players as Daniele De Rossi’s side won 2-0 at Sassuolo on Sunday, with Milutin Osmajić scoring both goals and the defence keeping a clean sheet.

That result made it three wins in four league games for the Grifone, who are 10th on 16 points.

Genoa will hope to have their defender back for a demanding week. They visit Inter at San Siro on Saturday at 20:45 CET [19:45 GMT], before facing the Nerazzurri again in the Coppa Italia next Tuesday.

#1206. Net zero emissions won’t reverse climate change — some nations look to ‘net negative’

Thank you for visiting nature.com. You are using a browser version with limited support for CSS. To obtain the best experience, we recommend you use a more up to date browser (or turn off compatibility mode in Internet Explorer). In the meantime, to ensure continued support, we are displaying the site without styles and JavaScript.

A display reminds those attending the COP31 climate summit in Antalya, Turkey, of their goal: limiting global warming to 1.5 ºC.Credit: Metin Aktas/Anadolu/Getty

Net zero is no longer enough. Among countries at the COP31 climate summit under way in Antalya, Turkey, there’s a growing recognition that meeting climate targets will require the world to go ‘net negative’, which means removal of more carbon dioxide from the air than is added.

Scientists say that climate ‘overshoot’ — exceeding 1.5 °C of warming, a target set in 2015 in the landmark Paris agreement — is now inevitable in the next few years. Reaching net-zero status would halt the rise in temperatures. But only achieving net-negative status can bring temperatures back below the 1.5 °C threshold this century.

Can AI actually help the climate? Nations want to harness the technology to cut emissions

Can AI actually help the climate? Nations want to harness the technology to cut emissions

That reality has made net negative and the enormous amount of CO2 removal that would be needed to achieve it a prominent idea at the summit. A coalition of eight countries called the Group of Negative Emitters (GONE) has been working to convince other nations to adopt net-negative targets and get serious about CO2 removal. The group announced that it will be co-chaired by Denmark and Ethiopia, which is hosting next year’s climate summit and could put net negative at the top of the agenda.

“We are in an era of overshoot, and we have to do a lot in terms of removing carbon dioxide,” Ethiopian ambassador Samuel Addis Alemayehu said at a GONE event on 18 November, touting the nation’s progress on reforestation.

Some climate campaigners worry that CO2 removal technologies won’t work and that focusing on them could distract countries from cutting emissions. Despite those concerns, the latest draft of the main statement from COP31 recognizes that CO2 removal has a role in addressing the overshoot, and welcomes efforts to “urgently and rapidly” scale up development of removal methods.

According to a United Nations Environment Programme (UNEP) report1 released ahead of the meeting, the world can expect about 1.8 °C of warming this century, even in the most optimistic emissions scenario.

Every fraction of a degree above 1.5 °C raises the risk of climate disasters such as wildfires and powerful hurricanes. “COP31 will be judged a failure if we don’t address the overshoot,” said Ilana Seid, Palau’s ambassador to the UN and chair of the Association of Small Island States, at a press briefing held during the summit.

Many countries at the meeting have discussed slashing emissions to limit the size and duration of the coming overshoot. Turkey has pushed to implement a target of 35% of global energy demand being met with electricity by 2035, a proposal that has gained support from more than 75 countries at the conference and is also included in the draft statement.

But the UNEP report estimates that to recover from overshoot, at least 330 billion tonnes of CO2 would have to be pulled out of the atmosphere this century after the world reaches net zero. Removing that much CO2 would require a vast expansion of existing efforts. Today, about two billion tonnes of CO2 per year are removed by nature-based projects such as reforestation, which takes advantage of the carbon absorbed by growing trees. Scaling up carbon removal quickly enough to achieve net negative and storing carbon in a more durable form will require technological CO2 removal solutions as well.

doi: https://doi.org/10.1038/d41586-026-03789-3
